description: platformAutomerge is off deliberately. It hands the merge to GitHub's native
auto-merge, which is faster, but with no branch protection configured GitHub will
happily merge a PR whose checks have not started yet — which would make the whole
'only when tests are green' arrangement a no-op. Renovate's own automerge waits
for the branch checks itself, at the cost of merging on its next run rather than
the instant CI goes green. Turn this back on if you add a branch protection rule
requiring the ci.yml checks.
minimumReleaseAge gives someone else three days to find a broken release before we
take it unattended; see the game-koi rule below for the one exemption.
ignoreTests is false, which is also the default — stated outright because it is the
one flag that would quietly turn the whole gate off. With it false, Renovate waits
for *passing* check runs: a branch with failing checks is never merged, and neither
is one where the checks never ran at all (absence is not treated as success).
The docs site's game-koi dependency is the reason this file exists.
docs/ installs the emulator from the npm registry rather than from the
workspace, so nothing in the build can sync that number: it has to name a
version that is already published. A caret range on a 0.x version admits
patch bumps only (^0.2.0 means >=0.2.0 <0.3.0), so every minor release used
to strand the docs on the old line with a build that still went green.
rangeStrategy replace so the range itself moves, not just the lockfile.
minimumReleaseAge 0 because the waiting period is there to let someone else
discover a bad release first, and there is no someone else for our own
package — we published it, and the point is that the docs follow promptly.
Automerge anything that is not a major, once CI is green. The gate is
.github/workflows/ci.yml: Renovate will not merge a branch whose checks are
failing or still running, so 'green' means the Rust workspace built, clippy
was clean, the unit tests passed, the npm package built and tested, and the
docs site built. What that does not cover is the Blargg/Mooneye ROM suites,
which skip themselves in CI because test-roms/ is gitignored — run
`just test-roms` locally after a batch of merges lands.
Majors stay manual. CI passing means it compiles and the tests pass, which is
exactly what a behavioural change in a renamed API also does. Note that Rust
0.x crates get their breaking changes as *minors* and are automerged above —
that is deliberate, since those do reliably fail to compile; the ones where a
silent behaviour change is plausible are pinned outright below.
egui, its two integration crates and pixels are one version set, not four
dependencies. The stats overlay borrows the wgpu Device and Queue that pixels
owns instead of creating its own, so both sides must compile against the same
wgpu: pixels 0.17.2 is on wgpu 29, and egui-wgpu 0.36 moved to wgpu 30.
Mismatching them links two semver-incompatible copies of wgpu and fails with
'expected wgpu::Device, found wgpu::Device'. Renovate cannot know which
combinations pair up, so it is left alone: move them together by hand and
check with `cargo tree -d`.
wasm-bindgen the crate must be the exact version of wasm-bindgen the CLI, or
the generated glue does not match the module's ABI. The CLI version lives in
three other places Renovate does not edit — build.sh, ci.yml and
npm-publish.yml's WASM_BINDGEN_VERSION — so a bump here alone would only trip
build.sh's own version check. Bump all four together by hand.
